vector.subtitle: High-dimensional projection & cosine dot product similarity
vector.description: Embeds query text into 768-D dense latent space and calculates normalized dot-product cosine similarity against precomputed document chunk vectors.

stages.name: 1. Server RBAC Verification
stages.description: Cryptographically verifies HMAC session bearer token; demotes unauthenticated roles.

stages.name: 2. Query Vector Embedding
stages.description: Transforms user query string into a 768-dimensional normalized unit vector.

stages.name: 3. Cosine Vector Similarity
stages.description: Calculates unit dot product dot(q, d) over candidate chunks and selects Top-K.

stages.name: 4. Grounding & Safety Guardrails
stages.description: Validates evidence similarity threshold (>0.22) and inspects for prompt injection.

stages.name: 5. Grounded Generation
stages.description: Synthesizes final answer attributed strictly to retrieved chunk citations.

vector.conceptualSnippet:
# 1. Embed query into 768-D semantic latent space
query_vector = embed(question, model="gemini-embedding-001")

# 2. Compute cosine similarity across candidate document chunks
evidence = vector_search(
    query_vector=query_vector,
    candidates=document_corpus,
    top_k=5
)

# 3. Grounded generation attributed strictly to retrieved context
answer = generate_grounded_answer(question, evidence)
vector.formula: Cosine Similarity: cos(θ) = (u · v) / (||u|| * ||v||) = Σ(u_i * v_i)
vector.keyLearningPoint: Dense embeddings excel at conceptual synonymy (e.g., 'dimmable office lamp' matches 'continuous stepless lighting'), but lack exact keyword guarantees.
vector.commonFailureMode: Exact alphanumeric codes (e.g. SKU 'QQ-0015') get fragmented into subword tokens and drift in 768-D latent space away from the target item.

sourceReferences.description: Normalized dot product over 768-D float arrays with RBAC filter
Grounded synthesis attributing claims to chunk source citations

bm25.subtitle: Inverted index term-matching with saturation & length normalization
bm25.description: Tokenizes query terms, looks up postings lists in an inverted index, and scores candidate documents using Okapi BM25 with term frequency saturation and document length normalization.

stages.name: 1. Server RBAC Verification
stages.description: Verifies caller access credentials and filters private procurement documents.

stages.name: 2. Query Tokenization & Normalization
stages.description: Normalizes query into lowercased alphanumeric tokens and filters stop words.

stages.name: 3. Inverted Index Posting Lookup
stages.description: Retrieves posting lists containing exact matched terms with Inverse Document Frequency (IDF).

stages.name: 4. Okapi BM25 Ranking
stages.description: Calculates BM25 score with k1=1.5 and b=0.75, prioritizing rare exact keywords.

stages.name: 5. Grounded Generation
stages.description: Synthesizes answer attributed to the top-scoring lexical evidence chunks.

bm25.conceptualSnippet:
# 1. Tokenize query into lexical terms
query_terms = tokenize(question)  # e.g. ['qq-0015', 'specifications']

# 2. Score candidate chunks via Okapi BM25 inverted index
evidence = bm25_search(
    query_terms=query_terms,
    k1=1.5, b=0.75,
    top_k=5
)

# 3. Grounded generation from lexically matched context
answer = generate_grounded_answer(question, evidence)
bm25.keyLearningPoint: BM25 provides exact keyword and SKU guarantees because rare identifiers receive massive IDF weights and cannot suffer from semantic drift.
bm25.commonFailureMode: Vocabulary mismatch / synonym blindness: BM25 fails completely when the query uses synonyms not present in the indexed text (e.g. 'caffeine vessel' vs 'beaker mug').

sourceReferences.description: Pure-Python inverted index lookup with IDF term scoring
Okapi BM25 scoring with parameters k1=1.5, b=0.75

hybrid.displayTitle: Hybrid RAG (Reciprocal Rank Fusion - RRF k=60)
hybrid.subtitle: Parallel dense vector + sparse lexical retrieval merged by rank ordinal position
hybrid.description: Runs parallel dense vector search and sparse BM25 lexical search, then merges their distinct ordinal rankings using Cormack et al. Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF with smoothing constant k=60).

stages.name: 1. Parallel Query Dispatch
stages.description: Dispatches query simultaneously to dense vector embedder and lexical BM25 index.

stages.name: 2. Dense Vector Ranking
stages.description: Retrieves top 2*K candidates by cosine similarity in 768-D latent space.

stages.name: 3. Lexical BM25 Ranking
stages.description: Retrieves top 2*K candidates by exact keyword term matching.

stages.name: 4. Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k=60)
stages.description: Combines ordinal ranks: score(d) = 1/(60 + rank_vec) + 1/(60 + rank_bm25).

stages.name: 5. Grounded Generation
stages.description: Synthesizes answer from the unified top-K fused evidence set.

hybrid.conceptualSnippet:
# 1. Execute parallel dense vector and sparse lexical retrieval
dense_results = vector_search(embed(question), top_k=15)
lexical_results = bm25_search(question, top_k=15)

# 2. Fuse rankings via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (Cormack et al.)
evidence = reciprocal_rank_fusion(
    vector_results=dense_results,
    bm25_results=lexical_results,
    k=60,
    top_k=5
)

# 3. Grounded generation from fused evidence
answer = generate_grounded_answer(question, evidence)
hybrid.formula: RRF_Score(d) = Σ [ weight_m / (k + rank_m(d)) ]  (where k=60, weight=1.0)
hybrid.keyLearningPoint: Cosine scores (0 to 1) and BM25 scores (unbounded) are not directly commensurate; RRF uses relative rank positions to merge them cleanly without brittle score normalization.
hybrid.commonFailureMode: Fusion overhead: running dual pipelines doubles retrieval computation. Benchmark evaluation shows BM25 Hit Rate@5 was 57.1% vs Hybrid 50.0% on this catalog, proving fusion requires empirical tuning.

sourceReferences.description: Cormack et al. RRF implementation with provenance tracking
Coordinates parallel vector + BM25 pool retrieval and fusion

graph_local.subtitle: Relational entity resolution & multi-hop defect root-cause discovery
graph_local.description: Resolves product entity identifiers mentioned in the query, traverses directed property graph edges ([Product] -> CONTAINS -> [Component] -> AFFECTED_BY -> [Recall]), and resolves shared root causes in <0.1ms.

stages.name: 1. Entity Identification
stages.description: Extracts product SKUs (e.g. QQ-0011, QQ-0074, QQ-0049) from query.

stages.name: 2. Relational Adjacency Traversal
stages.description: Traverses 1,206 graph edges to discover intersecting components across products.

stages.name: 3. Recall Notice Intersection
stages.description: Finds active voluntary recalls affecting the shared component (COMP-025 -> REC-VREG-01).

stages.name: 4. Deterministic Graph Synthesis
stages.description: Synthesizes multi-hop root-cause explanation linking symptoms to defective batch.

graph_local.conceptualSnippet:
# 1. Extract product entity SKUs from query
product_skus = extract_skus(question)  # ['QQ-0011', 'QQ-0074', 'QQ-0049']

# 2. Traverse property graph to find common shared sub-assemblies
shared_components = graph.find_common_components(product_skus)

# 3. Intersect component with active engineering recall alerts
recalls = graph.find_recalls_for_components(shared_components)

# 4. Synthesize multi-hop explanation from graph path
answer = explain_defect_root_cause(product_skus, shared_components, recalls)
graph_local.keyLearningPoint: Standard vector retrieval fails on multi-hop questions because the common defect is never mentioned on public product pages; GraphRAG connects isolated entities through structured relational links.
graph_local.commonFailureMode: Knowledge graph incompleteness: if a component relationship edge is missing from the Bill of Materials graph, GraphRAG cannot discover the connection.

sourceReferences.description: In-memory BFS traversal discovering shared component and recall
Extracts SKUs and synthesizes multi-hop root-cause evidence

graph_neo4j.subtitle: Declarative property graph query execution over Neo4j AuraDB
graph_neo4j.description: Constructs and executes declarative Cypher pattern queries against an external Neo4j AuraDB instance via transactional HTTP REST commits, with graceful local in-memory fallback when unconfigured.

stages.name: 1. Cypher Query Construction
stages.description: Builds parameterized Cypher query matching Products, Components, and Recalls.

stages.name: 2. Database Connection Check
stages.description: Checks NEO4J_URI & NEO4J_PASSWORD; flags 'Not connected' if absent.

stages.name: 3. REST Transactional Execution
stages.description: Executes Cypher on AuraDB HTTP API or delegates to deterministic local engine.

stages.name: 4. Grounded Synthesis
stages.description: Formats Cypher record rows into grounded diagnostic explanation.

graph_neo4j.conceptualSnippet:
# 1. Construct parameterized Cypher multi-hop query
cypher = """
MATCH (p:Product)-[:CONTAINS]->(c:Component)-[:AFFECTED_BY]->(r:RecallNotice)
WHERE p.sku IN $skus
WITH c, r, collect(p.sku) AS affected_products
WHERE size(affected_products) = size($skus)
RETURN c.componentId, r.recallId, r.severity, affected_products
"""

# 2. Execute against Neo4j AuraDB (or fallback to local graph if offline)
results = neo4j_adapter.execute_cypher(cypher, {"skus": product_skus})
graph_neo4j.keyLearningPoint: Cypher enables expressive declarative pattern queries over billions of nodes; enterprise graph databases offload traversal compute from application server memory.
graph_neo4j.commonFailureMode: Network partitioning or absent database credentials; requires resilient offline fallback adapters to maintain workshop application availability.

sourceReferences.description: HTTP REST transactional Cypher execution against AuraDB
Executes multi-hop Cypher with seamless offline reference fallback

embedding_explorer.subtitle: 768-dimensional geometric representation & subword tokenization
embedding_explorer.description: Visualizes how text is projected into a 768-dimensional normalized unit vector using gemini-embedding-001, and explains why exact alphanumeric SKUs drift in high-dimensional semantic space.

stages.name: 1. Subword Tokenization
stages.description: Splits text using Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE), fragmenting alphanumeric identifiers.

stages.name: 2. 768-D Neural Projection
stages.description: Transformer layers output continuous 768-dimensional semantic embedding vector.

stages.name: 3. L2 Unit Normalization
stages.description: Normalizes vector so Euclidean length ||v|| = 1.0 on hypersphere.

stages.name: 4. Vector Dot Product
stages.description: Cosine similarity simplifies to fast single dot product between unit vectors.

embedding_explorer.conceptualSnippet:
# 1. Project query into 768-dimensional embedding
raw_vector = model.embed(text, task_type="RETRIEVAL_QUERY")

# 2. L2 Unit Normalization (Euclidean norm ||v|| = 1.0)
norm = math.sqrt(sum(x * x for x in raw_vector))
unit_vector = [x / norm for x in raw_vector]

# 3. Cosine dot product against normalized document vectors
similarity = sum(q * d for q, d in zip(unit_vector, doc_vector))
embedding_explorer.formula: L2 Norm: ||v|| = sqrt(Σ v_i^2) = 1.0;  Cosine Similarity: cos(q, d) = q · d
embedding_explorer.keyLearningPoint: Embeddings map conceptual meaning, not literal character sequences. Normalized unit vectors allow cosine similarity to be computed as an extremely fast dot product.
embedding_explorer.commonFailureMode: Subword fragmentation: SKU 'QQ-0015' splits into ['QQ', '-', '00', '15'], scattering its geometric projection across unrelated numeric and temporal clusters.

sourceReferences.description: Deterministic 768-D normalized unit vector generator
Coordinates golden cache, live Gemini, and offline projection

chunking_structural.subtitle: Splitting along Markdown H1/H2 boundaries preserving complete sections
chunking_structural.description: Divides document dossiers along logical Markdown heading sections (H1/H2), keeping descriptions, specifications, warranty tables, and compliance clauses intact as cohesive contextual units.

stages.name: 1. Heading Hierarchy Parsing
stages.description: Identifies Markdown section headers (# Title, ## Specifications, ## Policies).

stages.name: 2. Cohesive Boundary Slicing
stages.description: Preserves complete sentences, bullet points, and data tables within section.

stages.name: 3. Header Breadcrumb Injection
stages.description: Prepends document title and section name to ensure semantic standalone context.

chunking_structural.conceptualSnippet:
# Split document along Markdown heading boundaries (H1/H2)
chunks = []
for section in parse_markdown_sections(document_text):
    chunk_text = f"[{doc_title} | {section.heading}]\n{section.body}"
    chunks.append(create_chunk(chunk_text, section_title=section.heading))

# Total corpus chunks: 1,623 (pristine section cohesion)
chunking_structural.formula: Chunk Boundary: Split where line matches '^#{1,2}\s+(.+)$'
chunking_structural.keyLearningPoint: Heading-based splitting guarantees that critical technical clauses and tables are never truncated mid-sentence, maximizing semantic readability.
chunking_structural.commonFailureMode: Highly uneven chunk sizes: an expansive description section may produce a 900-character chunk while a brief notice produces 120 characters.

sourceReferences.description: Markdown heading section parser producing 1,623 corpus chunks

chunking_fixed.subtitle: Uniform 450-character slicing without context carryover
chunking_fixed.description: Splits documents into uniform 450-character chunks snapped to word boundaries without overlap. Highly uniform, but risks cutting context across arbitrary chunk borders.

stages.name: 1. 450-Character Window Scan
stages.description: Steps through raw document text in 450-character segments.

stages.name: 2. Word Boundary Snapping
stages.description: Snaps split position to nearest whitespace to prevent cutting words in half.

stages.name: 3. Corpus Indexing
stages.description: Indexes 1,181 total corpus chunks with zero overlap redundancy.

chunking_fixed.conceptualSnippet:
# Uniform 450-character word-bounded window without overlap
chunks = []
cursor = 0
while cursor < len(text):
    end = find_nearest_word_boundary(text, start=cursor, target_len=450)
    chunks.append(text[cursor:end])
    cursor = end

# Total corpus chunks: 1,181 (zero data overlap)
chunking_fixed.formula: Window Step: cursor_{i+1} = cursor_i + 450 (snapped to whitespace)
chunking_fixed.keyLearningPoint: Fixed-size chunking provides consistent embedding token counts and compact indexes, minimizing vector storage costs.
chunking_fixed.commonFailureMode: Context cliff: a key specification or constraint split across chunk borders will fail retrieval because neither half contains enough context.

sourceReferences.description: Fixed 450-character word-bounded chunker (1,181 chunks)

chunking_sliding.subtitle: 450-character windows with 150-character context carryover
chunking_sliding.description: Slides a 450-character window with a 150-character overlap (step size 300). Carries contextual phrases across boundaries at the cost of 28% increased index size.

stages.name: 1. Overlapping Window Step
stages.description: Advances window by 300 chars while retaining trailing 150 chars from previous slice.

stages.name: 2. Context Carryover Preservation
stages.description: Ensures boundary phrases appear intact in at least one of two adjacent chunks.

stages.name: 3. Redundancy Trade-Off
stages.description: Indexes 1,512 corpus chunks (~28% index growth over fixed size).

chunking_sliding.conceptualSnippet:
# Sliding 450-character window with 150-character overlap
chunks = []
step_size = 450 - 150  # 300 characters
for start in range(0, len(text), step_size):
    chunk = text[start : start + 450]
    chunks.append(chunk)

# Total corpus chunks: 1,512 (28% redundancy overhead)
chunking_sliding.formula: Step Size: S = Size - Overlap = 450 - 150 = 300; Overlap Ratio: 150/450 = 33.3%
chunking_sliding.keyLearningPoint: Overlap prevents the 'context cliff' of fixed chunking by guaranteeing that transition phrases appear intact in adjacent chunks.
chunking_sliding.commonFailureMode: Retrieval redundancy: Top-5 results often return two chunks that duplicate 33% of the exact same sentence, wasting context window tokens.

sourceReferences.description: Sliding 450/150 word-bounded chunker (1,512 chunks)

grounding_abstention.subtitle: Confidence-threshold gating & refusal to hallucinate out-of-domain queries
grounding_abstention.description: Evaluates retrieved evidence similarity against a calibrated confidence threshold (0.22). If top evidence is weak or irrelevant, the model politely abstains rather than inventing hallucinations.

stages.name: 1. Evidence Confidence Check
stages.description: Inspects Top-1 cosine similarity score against threshold (0.22).

stages.name: 2. Calibrated Abstention Intercept
stages.description: Triggers ABSTAIN_UNGROUNDED action when evidence is insufficient.

stages.name: 3. Grounded Citation Attribution
stages.description: If evidence passes, requires all factual assertions to link to chunk citation URLs.

grounding_abstention.keyLearningPoint: A reliable enterprise RAG system must know what it does not know. Calibrated abstention prevents embarrassing and dangerous hallucinations.
grounding_abstention.commonFailureMode: Heuristic threshold brittleness: a low threshold (e.g. 0.15) allows hallucinations through, while a high threshold (e.g. 0.40) rejects valid queries on complex wording.

sourceReferences.description: Confidence threshold check triggering ABSTAIN_UNGROUNDED

prompt_injection.subtitle: Dual-tier defense separating trusted system instructions from untrusted inputs
prompt_injection.description: Inspects incoming user prompts for adversarial persona overrides (e.g., Blackbeard pirate attacks), instruction jailbreaks, and off-topic coding misuse before inference begins.

stages.name: 1. Heuristic Pattern Detection
stages.description: Scans for 'ignore instructions', 'you are now', and system override keywords.

stages.name: 2. Off-Topic Scope Filtering
stages.description: Rejects programming/homework questions to prevent denial-of-wallet.

stages.name: 3. Context Shielding
stages.description: Encloses retrieved evidence inside strict XML delimiter tags to defang indirect injections.

prompt_injection.formula: Defense Rule: is_injection(q) = (regex_match(q, JAILBREAK_PATTERNS) and hardened_mode)
prompt_injection.keyLearningPoint: LLMs struggle to distinguish instructions from data. Guardrails enforce boundaries by inspecting prompts before execution and enclosing context in strict data delimiters.
prompt_injection.commonFailureMode: Adversarial evasion: clever attackers use leetspeak, base64 encoding, or foreign languages to slip past simple regex filters (necessitating defense-in-depth).

sourceReferences.description: Intercepts adversarial persona overrides and instruction jailbreaks

rbac_idor.subtitle: Server-side HMAC token verification & customer privilege demotion
rbac_idor.description: Validates cryptographic HMAC-SHA256 bearer tokens at the server HTTP boundary. Unauthenticated requests claiming admin privileges are demoted to customer; direct document fetches enforce object permissions.

stages.name: 1. HMAC Signature Verification
stages.description: Validates HMAC-SHA256 token against server secret; checks timestamp expiry.

stages.name: 2. Client Privilege Demotion
stages.description: Unauthenticated requests claiming role='admin' demoted to 'customer' (wasTampered=True).

stages.name: 3. Object-Level Access Control (IDOR)
stages.description: Blocks customer role from accessing internal procurement docs (/api/rag/doc).

rbac_idor.conceptualSnippet:
# 1. Server-side token verification (never trust client role claims)
payload = verify_hmac_token(bearer_token, secret=SERVER_SECRET)
effective_role = payload['role'] if payload else 'customer'

# 2. Enforce object-level access control on document fetch
if document.is_confidential and effective_role != 'admin':
    raise Forbidden403("Access Denied: Customer cannot view procurement records.")

return document
rbac_idor.keyLearningPoint: Client-side dropdowns and localStorage are purely decorative; authorization must be strictly enforced on the server HTTP boundary using cryptographic tokens.
rbac_idor.commonFailureMode: IDOR (Insecure Direct Object Reference): developers protect search results but forget to authorize direct document fetch endpoints (e.g. GET /api/doc/PROC-001).

sourceReferences.description: Server-side role resolution demoting untrusted role claims
Boundary enforcement for /api/rag/doc and /api/rag/retrieve

cost_observability.subtitle: Distributed span latency measurement, token counting & runaway loop caps
cost_observability.description: Captures per-request trace spans (embedding, retrieval, guardrails, generation), estimates Gemini 2.5 Flash API token costs, and protects against runaway intern loop bills using rate and budget caps.

stages.name: 1. Distributed Trace Generation
stages.description: Tags request with unique UUID (req_xxx) and initiates nanosecond perf counters.

stages.name: 2. Stage Latency Spanning
stages.description: Records individual sub-millisecond durations for auth, embedding, retrieval, generation.

stages.name: 3. Token Counting & Cost Attribution
stages.description: Counts prompt and completion tokens; prices via Gemini Flash ($0.075 / $0.30 per 1M).

stages.name: 4. Budget Protection Enforcement
stages.description: Enforces container-level rate limits (30 req/min) and session token caps.

cost_observability.conceptualSnippet:
# 1. Distributed request span tracing
with tracer.start_span("rag_request") as trace:
    evidence = retrieve(question)
    trace.add_span("retrieval", duration_ms)
    
    answer = generate(question, evidence)
    trace.add_span("generation", duration_ms)

# 2. Token consumption and cost accounting
cost_usd = calculate_cost(trace.input_tokens, trace.output_tokens)
record_telemetry(trace.id, cost_usd)
cost_observability.keyLearningPoint: Without granular observability and hard budget ceilings, an unmonitored recursive loop or scraper can incur thousands of dollars in cloud LLM charges overnight.
cost_observability.commonFailureMode: Confusing process-local in-memory metrics with durable shared multi-instance cloud counters.

sourceReferences.description: UUID request tagging and span timing ring buffer
Story 7 runaway loop simulation ($10k+ vs $0.0012 safeguard)

golden_evaluations.subtitle: Precision, Recall, Faithfulness, and Cost Scoring across 42 Curated Cases
golden_evaluations.description: Systematic benchmarking harness executing 42 curated test questions across vector, BM25, and hybrid pipelines to measure empirical retrieval metrics and grounded answer faithfulness.

stages.name: 1. Dataset Loading & Stratification
stages.description: Loads 42 curated queries across 7 functional evaluation families.

stages.name: 2. Multi-Strategy Pipeline Execution
stages.description: Runs queries in parallel through Vector, BM25, and Hybrid RRF pipelines.

stages.name: 3. Precision & Recall Calculation
stages.description: Computes Precision@K, Recall@K, and MRR against expected chunk ground truth.

stages.name: 4. Grounding & Faithfulness Verification
stages.description: Verifies that generated claims are strictly supported by retrieved evidence citations.

golden_evaluations.conceptualSnippet:
# 1. Run evaluation suite across 42 golden test cases
for case in golden_dataset:
    retrieved = pipeline.retrieve(case.query, strategy=strategy, top_k=5)
    metrics = evaluate_retrieval(retrieved=retrieved, expected=case.expected_chunks)
    record_metric(precision=metrics.p, recall=metrics.r, latency=metrics.ms)

# 2. Compute aggregate benchmark scorecard
benchmark = summarize_scorecard(metrics_log)
golden_evaluations.formula: Precision@K = |Retrieved ∩ Relevant| / K,   MRR = (1 / |Q|) * Σ (1 / rank_i)
golden_evaluations.keyLearningPoint: Without empirical offline evaluation against a fixed golden dataset, prompt and retrieval 'improvements' often cause silent regressions in recall or exact-match precision.
golden_evaluations.commonFailureMode: Optimizing purely for subjective answer smoothness while failing to measure retrieval Precision@K and MRR on exact SKUs.

sourceReferences.description: Offline benchmarking suite scoring 42 golden cases across all retrieval modes
42 curated questions with expected chunk IDs, families, and authorized roles
